title: Fact-check report
description: Contract between the analysis (produced by the verifier) and the HTML report template. The JSON must validate against this schema AND satisfy every rule in x-invariants, which scripts/render.py checks before rendering.

checked_at.description: When the check ran; sources were read at this time.

language.description: Report language, same as the user's (e.g. it). Drives UI labels and all generated text.

scope.description: selection = passage quoted by the user; full_response = whole previous answer.

verifier_mode.description: independent_agent = separate agent with no conversation context; same_session_refetch = same session, every page re-fetched. Shown in the report footer.

original_had_citations.description: false if the original text cited no sources and the verifier searched for new ones.

status.description: Must equal the status recomputed by rule V1 in x-invariants.

headline.description: One plain-language sentence explaining the verdict, in meta.language.

basis.description: Claims that triggered the verdict rule. Empty only when status = reliable.

segments.description: The text split in order. Concatenating every segment's text must reproduce original exactly. No numeric offsets: models count characters badly.

text.description: Identical to the text of its segment.

kind.description: synthesis and opinion are the model's own content and cannot be checked against a source.

critical.description: true if the user would base a decision on it, or if it is a number or a surprising claim. Always true for kind = number; never true for synthesis or opinion (rule C12).

critical_reason.description: Required when critical = true, otherwise null.

reason.description: Why it got this outcome, in one line, in meta.language.

issues.description: Typical errors found. Empty when supported or not_checkable.

cited_source_ids.description: Sources the original answer attached to this claim.

relation.description: qualifies = the source confirms only in part, or with caveats the text dropped.

excerpt.description: Passage copied verbatim from the source, max 15 words, in the SOURCE's language: never translated.

deep_link.description: Source URL with a text fragment pointing at the excerpt.

independent_source_count.description: Number of distinct origin groups among the sources of evidence with relation = supports.

url.description: The page URL, without any #anchor (deep links append #:~:text= to it).

published_at.description: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD; null if the page is undated.

cited_in_original.description: false = found by the verifier during corroboration.

type.description: primary = original data, study or document; secondary = reports on it; aggregator = collects third-party content; low_quality = SEO or generated content, or no verifiable author.

lateral_check.description: What at least one source outside the page says about the publisher or author.

origin_groups.description: Every source belongs to exactly one group. An original, independent source is a group on its own; sources repeating the same origin (e.g. the same press release) share a group.

label.description: The shared origin, e.g. 'Press release of 13/03/2023'.

text.description: One concrete action, verb first, in meta.language.

issue.description: citation_mismatch = the cited source does not contain the claim; number_distorted = rounding, unit or year changed; hedge_dropped = caveats lost; overgeneralized = a specific case turned into a rule; misattributed = attributed to the wrong author; sources_merged = combines two sources into a claim neither supports alone; outdated = old figure presented as current; source_unreachable = source could not be read.

x-invariants.description: Rules JSON Schema cannot express. scripts/render.py checks all of them; if one fails, the verifier fixes the JSON and retries. Never render a JSON that breaks them.
text: T1. Concatenating text.segments[].text reproduces text.original exactly, character by character.
T2. Every claim appears in exactly one segment, and that segment's text equals claims[].text.
T3. Every claim_id in segments, verdict.basis and follow_ups points to an existing claim.
claims: C1. Claim ids are unique and numbered in order of appearance (c1, c2, ...).
C2. kind in {synthesis, opinion} <=> outcome = not_checkable. In that case evidence, issues and cited_source_ids are empty.
C3. critical = true => critical_reason is not null; critical = false => critical_reason = null.
C4. outcome = supported => at least one evidence with relation = supports, none with relation = contradicts, issues empty.
C5. outcome = partial => at least one evidence with relation = qualifies, or issues not empty.
C6. outcome = contradicted => at least one evidence with relation = contradicts.
C7. outcome = unsupported => no evidence with relation = supports.
C8. outcome = unverifiable => every source in cited_source_ids has access.status = failed, and issues contains source_unreachable.
C9. independent_source_count = number of distinct origin_group_id among sources of evidence with relation = supports.
C10. Every excerpt has at most 15 words, the deep link's text fragment is part of it, and (with render.py --pages) it appears verbatim in the saved page text.
C11. deep_link = the url of the source named in source_id, without any #anchor, followed directly by #:~:text=.
C12. kind = number => critical = true; kind in {synthesis, opinion} => critical = false.
sources: S1. Source ids are unique; every source_id referenced elsewhere exists.
S2. Every source appears in exactly one origin_group, and origin_group_id matches that group.
S4. Every source is used by at least one claim (in cited_source_ids or in evidence).
verdict: V0. counts matches the tally of outcomes in claims.
V1. status is recomputed with the rules below, evaluated in order; it must equal the declared status.

1. problematic: at least one critical claim with outcome in {unsupported, contradicted}, OR at least one critical claim whose supporting evidence (relation = supports) comes only from sources with reliability.level = low.

2. reliable: at least one claim has outcome = supported; every critical claim has outcome = supported and independent_source_count >= 2; no claim has outcome in {contradicted, unsupported, unverifiable}; no supported claim relies only on low-reliability sources.
3. needs_review: every other case (including: no checkable claim).
V2. verdict.basis lists the claims that triggered the applied rule; it is empty only when status = reliable.
render: R1. The template shows by default: verdict, annotated text, sources, omissions, follow-ups. Claim cards start collapsed.
R2. Visible labels are translated into meta.language through a label dictionary in the template (e.g. needs_review -> 'Da verificare' in Italian). Excerpts are never translated.
